column2: BULK UPLOAD VERSION 3.1 — Please DO NOT EDIT this cell.

At 4:52 on Friday my laptop was still open and my boss was still typing. I could see the three little dots. I made a decision. I walked down the hall, unhooked the bra, and tossed it over the bedroom door like a white flag. Then I came back and answered his email from the recliner in my fuzzy socks, and honestly it was the best work I did all week. He'll never know. Nobody on Monday's video call will know either. The camera only goes down so far, and so do my standards after five.
column6: My sister calls it the five o'clock drop. She says she can hear it over the phone, the little sigh I make when the hooks let go. I told her that's not a sigh. That's the sound of the workday officially ending. She says the same thing happens at her house.

column2: Tuesday it was the way the bagger put the bread under the cans. Wednesday it was a man in the bank parking lot who backed into his spot. Thursday, and I want to be clear about this, it was a perfectly nice woman humming in the elevator. I didn't see any of them coming. Neither did they. My husband has started checking my face when I walk in the door, like a weatherman reading the radar. Some days he gets it right. Most days he just says hi from across the room and lets me find out on my own.
column6: Last week I got mad at a dish towel. Not a person, not a situation, a dish towel that wouldn't hang straight on the oven handle. I folded it three different ways and then threw it in the sink. My daughter asked what the towel did. I'm still working on that answer.

column2: Saturday morning at Kroger, 8:15, the parking lot was nearly empty and the cart corral was full. Fifty carts, all lined up and shiny. I picked one from the middle like a woman who knows what she's doing. By the bananas it had started squeaking. By the bread it was pulling left so hard I was basically steering a canoe. A man by the deli watched me fight it all the way down aisle seven and nodded like he'd been there. I didn't trade it in. At this point we have history. I think it waits for me all week.
column6: My husband swears it's my technique. So last month I sent him in for milk and watched from the car. Ten minutes later he came out pushing a cart that rattled so loud people turned around. He has not mentioned my technique since.

column2: Monday at 8:02 I walked into the break room carrying my coffee and my whole personality. Margaret from accounting said good morning, and I told her exactly what I thought of the morning. Pleasantly. With a smile. By 9:30 I had a calendar invite from HR titled Quick Chat. It was not quick. There was a handout. Apparently there's a list of approved greetings, and mine is not on it. I read the whole list. Rise and shine was on there. Nobody has ever risen and shined in that building. At least mine is honest.
column6: In fairness, the copier jammed four times before nine that morning and the Wi-Fi was down until lunch. Margaret came by my desk around eleven, set a donut down, and said you weren't wrong. Then she went back to her desk without another word. I'm keeping her.
